A previously healthy 15-year-old boy presents to the emergency department in cardiac arrest.
The patient’s laboratory studies were unremarkable from a visit to the pediatrician 3 weeks ago.
His teacher began chest compressions and he has received epinephrine and defibrillation from paramedics while in transport.
An autopsy is performed and is notable for no clear abnormalities.
He was in class when he suddenly fainted and became unresponsive.
On arrival, the patient remains pulseless and is pronounced dead.
